head: pr17398-r19
report:
I found three defects that should be fixed before merge. All three come from one change: `gc --archive` now keeps the live copy. But `materializeSessionFile`, which runs on every `SessionManager` open and fork, and `copySessionIntoArchive` still treat any difference between the live artifact tree and the archive as either an interrupted restore or a conflict. A session that simply carried on after archiving falls into both cases.

I reproduced each one with probes in the scratch dir (`probe.test.ts`, `probe2.test.ts`), run from `packages/coding-agent`. The shared fixture is an idle v3 session `…_01a18630-….jsonl` with an artifact `<artifacts>/1.bash.log` = `"tool output\n"`. It is aged 30 days and archived with `runGcCommand({archive:true, apply:true, coldArchiveAfterDays:0, retainNewest*:0})`. The result is `archived:1, errors:[]`, and the live copy is kept.

## 1. If a live artifact changes after archiving, the session can no longer be opened, and the suggested fix loops

**Mechanism.** `SessionManager.setSessionFile` → `materializeSessionFile` finds the retained archive beside the live `.jsonl`. It then calls `liveSessionIsComplete` (`session-archive.ts:1217`). That check returns `false` when a live counterpart is missing, is not a regular file, or is empty while the archived file isn't. On `false`, it runs `restoreArchivedSession` → `copyTreeDereferenced`, which refuses because the live file "already holds something else". `materializeSessionFile` then throws. The session was never reclaimed and its live copy is complete, yet the open fails.

**Trigger.** Archive the fixture, run `Bun.write(<artifacts>/1.bash.log, "")`, then `SessionManager.open(sessionFile)`.

**Measured.** The open fails on both attempts:
```
T3.1 open failed: Restored the transcript of ".../archive/sessions/--work--/…jsonl.gz" to …jsonl, but could not restore the artifact tree … 1.bash.log already holds something else…
T3.2 open failed: (same)
```
Resume, fork, `render`, `session pack` and `anonymize` all go through the same path, so all of them fail the same way.

**The re-archive path also refuses.** Rewrite the artifact with different bytes (`"different\n"`) and run `--archive --apply` again. It refuses with "the archive already holds …1.bash.log, and it is not what archiving … would write … Bring the session home with `omp gc --restore <id> --apply` and archive it again". Running that `--restore` gives `artifactsRestored:false` with the same "already holds something else" error, and the next `--archive` still has `errors.length === 1`. The printed remedy never terminates.

The code's own comment (lines 1199–1203) says "a tool rewrites its output" is ordinary living that must not be read as an interrupted restore. Line 76 of the CHANGELOG says a restored session "can be archived again once it advances". The probes show both claims are false.

## 2. Opening or forking a session you own fails when any live artifact differs from the archive

**Mechanism.** Same path as #1. When `liveSessionIsComplete` is false, `restoreArchivedSession` → `tryAcquireRestoreLeases` needs the session's own lease. A caller that already holds it is refused. The comment at line 1267 says this exact failure ("an ordinary fork of a session the caller already owns fail[s] with 'a running process owns this session'") was fixed. It was fixed only for the case where every archived artifact still has a live counterpart.

**Trigger.** Archive the fixture, `fs.rm(<artifacts>/1.bash.log)`, take `tryAcquireSessionLease(ID)`, then call `SessionManager.open(sessionFile)` and `SessionManager.forkFrom(sessionFile, "/tmp")`.

**Measured.**
```
open failed: Cannot restore "…jsonl.gz": a running process owns this session or one of its subagent sessions. Close it and run `omp gc --restore 01a18630-… --apply --agent-dir …` again.
fork failed: (same)
```
The message tells the user to close the owner, but the owner is the caller itself.

## 3. Opening a session brings back artifacts that were deleted or renamed after archiving

**Mechanism.** Same check. A deleted or renamed artifact has no live counterpart at the archived relative path. The open therefore runs a restore, which `link`s the archived file back into the live tree.

**Trigger and measured.**
- `fs.rm(<artifacts>/1.bash.log)`, then `SessionManager.open(sessionFile)`: the live artifacts go from `[]` to `["1.bash.log"]`. The deleted tool output is back.
- `fs.rename(1.bash.log → 2.bash.log)`, then open: the live artifacts are `["2.bash.log", "1.bash.log"]`, so the file is duplicated under its old name.

For a renamed subagent transcript, this produces a second copy of the child session in the artifact tree. The comment at line 1200 names "a child renames itself" as the case this check must accept.

**Fix direction for #1–#3.** While a live transcript exists, opening it should not depend on whether its artifacts match the archive's. Only an interrupted restore needs finishing, and it should be identified by an explicit restore-in-progress marker, not inferred from per-file presence. Re-archiving should replace archived artifacts the live tree has superseded, as it already does for the transcript prefix, instead of refusing.

---

I did not review most of the reclaim and staging code in `gc-cli.ts`, the `Settings.loadReadOnly` legacy-JSON change, or the archive-scope fallback in `resolveResumableSession` in depth within the time limit.
